title: e.l.f. Beauty (ELF) Up 16.4% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
author: Zacks.Com
description: e.l.f. Beauty shares surged 16.4% following a strong Q1 earnings beat driven by exceptional Rhode brand momentum and international growth. The company raised its fiscal 2027 guidance to 18-20% sales growth and $3.50-$3.55 EPS. However, post-earnings estimate revisions have trended downward by 21.54%, and the stock carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating with expectations for in-line returns ahead.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While the company delivered strong Q1 earnings with a 36% sales beat, raised full-year guidance, and benefited from Rhode momentum, post-earnings estimate revisions have declined 21.54%. The Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating and expectation for in-line returns suggest limited upside despite recent stock appreciation, indicating the positive catalysts may already be priced in.

title: e.l.f. Beauty Stock: Buy or Sell?
author: Parkev Tatevosian, Cfa
description: e.l.f. Beauty is experiencing booming sales but faces rising marketing expenses. The stock has declined 53% from its all-time high, raising questions about whether the sell-off is an overreaction. Management is aggressively pursuing market share gains, with the company recently benefiting from the Rhode brand surge.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Despite a 53% decline from all-time highs, the company shows booming sales and aggressive market share expansion strategy. The Motley Fool recommends the stock, and recent performance (Rhode brand surge) suggests potential recovery. The sell-off appears to be viewed as an overreaction by analysts.

title: e.l.f. Beauty Is Down 53% From Its All-Time High. Is the Sell-Off an Overreaction?
author: Leo Sun
description: e.l.f. Beauty's stock has declined 53% from its March 2024 all-time high of $221.83 to around $105, driven by slowing revenue growth, higher operating expenses, and supply chain challenges. While the stock appears cheap at 17x adjusted EBITDA, the company's high-growth days are over as it matures, with analysts projecting only 20% revenue growth in fiscal 2027 and 8% in fiscal 2028. The sell-off may not be an overreaction given the company's deceleration and lack of catalysts for near-term appreciation.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The company faces slowing organic growth, increased operating expenses from tariffs and inflationary pressures, and maturing business fundamentals. Despite appearing cheap on valuation metrics, the analyst expects stock stagnation without acceleration in organic growth.

title: Amazon.com vs. e.l.f. Beauty: Which High-Growth Consumer Stock Is a Better Investment in 2026?
author: Robert Izquierdo
description: The article compares Amazon.com and e.l.f. Beauty as high-growth consumer stocks. Amazon generates $716.9B in revenue with a 10.8% net margin and $7.7B free cash flow, while e.l.f. Beauty shows faster growth at 24.6% year-over-year with $1.6B revenue but only 1.6% net margin. The author recommends Amazon due to its attractive forward P/E ratio (20.7x vs 29.3x), strong AWS growth (37% YoY), and AI infrastructure investments, despite e.l.f. Beauty's higher growth rate.

Lower forward P/E ratio (20.7x) suggests attractive valuation despite record stock price. Author's recommendation to buy in 2026.

title: Coupang vs. e.l.f. Beauty: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Sara Appino
description: The article compares two consumer growth stocks: Coupang, a South Korean e-commerce and logistics giant with 25 million users, and e.l.f. Beauty, a viral cosmetics brand. While Coupang trades at a lower valuation (P/S 0.8x), e.l.f. Beauty is recommended as the better buy due to its 30-quarter growth streak, strong earnings beat, successful Rhode acquisition, and accelerating momentum. Coupang faces headwinds including a major data breach affecting 33 million accounts, regulatory fines, and currency weakness.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While the company shows steady revenue growth (14.1% YoY) and profitability, it faces significant headwinds including a major data breach compromising 33 million accounts, regulatory fines, currency weakness, and geopolitical risks. The author notes it is 'managing headwinds' rather than accelerating.

The company demonstrates strong momentum with 30 consecutive quarters of sales growth (24.6% YoY), a significant earnings beat, successful Rhode acquisition integration, surging international revenue, and market share gains. The author explicitly recommends it as 'the stronger pick' for long-term investors due to accelerating growth and brand momentum.
